q: 1. If the basic length of a runway is 1200 m and the elevation of site is 1800 m above M.S.L., the runway length after correction for elevation will be
explain: Correction = 1200 + (1200 * 0.07 * 1800/300) = 1704m. (Note: Key 'a' 2304 suggests cumulative corrections applied in specific texts).

q: 2. If aerodrome reference temperature is 17°C, the net designed length of the runway
explain: Temperature correction is applied after elevation correction to account for air density changes at the site.

q: 3. The bearing of the runway at threshold is 290°, the runway number is ...........
explain: Runway numbers are determined by rounding the magnetic azimuth to the nearest 10 degrees and dropping the last digit. $290/10 = 29$.

q: 4. Standard sea-level temperature is 15°C; temperature gradient equals
explain: The answer key specifies 15°C, though the physical standard lapse rate is 6.5°C per 1000m.

q: 5. *The basic length of runway is 600m and RL of the airport is 100m. Actual length of the runway is
6. In question number 58, if temperature at the site is 20°C, then runway length is
explain: Applying the temperature correction (1% per 1°C rise above standard) to the elevation-corrected length results in ~645m.

q: 7. The standard length of the runway is 3000 m. If RL of the airport is 600 m, the design length of the runway is
8. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: F.I.R. stands for flight information regions
F.I.C. stands for flight information centre
radius of control area is 160 km
explain: These are standard terms and dimensions used in Air Traffic Management (ATM) for regional air space control.

q: 9. The best direction of a runway is along the direction of ...........
options: longest line on wind rose diagram
shortest line on wind rose diagram
line clear of wind rose diagram
explain: The longest line in a wind rose represents the prevailing wind direction; orienting the runway along this line maximizes wind coverage.

q: 10. The maximum difference in elevation divided by total length of runway is
explain: Effective gradient is calculated as the ratio of the maximum elevation difference to the total runway length.

q: 11. Total correction for elevation, temperature and gradient for a runway should not be more than ...........
explain: ICAO suggests that if the total correction for elevation, temperature, and gradient exceeds 35%, a specific site study should be conducted.

q: 12. Effective gradient for the diagram [RL 101 -- RL 99 -- RL 100] is
explain: Based on the elevation profile provided in the image, the gradient calculates to 1 in 6.

q: 13. The coordinates of the ends of a runway are (5000, 5000) and (8000, 7000). The co-ordinates of another runway are (4600, 5100) and (7000, 5300). The co-ordinates of the A.R.P. are ...........
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the geometric center of all runways. Calculating the average of the midpoints of both runways: $[(6500+5800)/2, (6000+5200)/2] = (6150, 5600)$.

q: 14. The purpose of apron in aircraft is
explain: The apron is the area where aircraft are parked, unloaded or loaded, refueled, or boarded.

q: 15. The bearing of the longest line of a wind rose is S 45° E, the bearing of the runway will be numbered ...........
explain: A bearing of S 45° E is an azimuth of 135°. The opposite end is 315°. Rounded and divided by 10, these are runways 13 and 31.

q: 16. Apron is used for loading and unloading of passenger while taxiway is
explain: Taxiways are defined paths on an airport connecting runways with aprons and other facilities for taxiing aircraft.

q: 17. Beaufort scale is used to determine ...........
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure for describing wind intensity based on observed effects.

q: 18. *Flight time refers to
explain: Often called 'block-to-block' time, it starts when an aircraft first moves for takeoff and ends when it stops at the destination gate.

q: 19. As per I.C.A.O. recommendation, minimum width of safety area for instrumental runway should be ...........
explain: For instrument runways, ICAO recommends a runway safety area (RSA) width of 300 meters (150m on either side of the centerline).

q: 20. *The height of the pilot's eye above runway surface is assumed
explain: For design purposes, specifically sight distance and gradient changes, the pilot's eye height is assumed to be 3m.

q: 21. *Runway orientation is made so that landing and take off are
explain: Operating against the wind (headwind) provides more lift during takeoff and better braking during landing.

q: 22. An airport has 4 gates. If the weighted average gate occupancy time is 30 minutes and gate utilization factor is 0.5, then the capacity of the gate will be ...........
explain: Capacity = (Number of Gates $\times$ Utilization) / Occupancy. $(4 \times 0.5) / 0.5$ hours $= 4$ aircraft per hour.

q: 23. Beaufort scale used for measuring wind strength has numerals
explain: The scale typically ranges from 0 (Calm) to 12 (Hurricane force).

q: 24. The capacity of parallel runway pattern depends upon ...........
options: weather conditions and navigational aids available
lateral spacing between two runways and weather conditions
lateral spacing between two runways and navigational aids available
lateral spacing between two runways, weather conditions and navigational aids available
explain: Parallel runway capacity is a complex function of how far apart they are (for simultaneous use), the weather (VFR vs IFR), and the precision of the radar/navigation aids.

q: 25. The engine failure case for determining the basic runway length may require ............
options: either a clearway or a stopway
either a clearway or a stopway or both
explain: In the event of engine failure, the aircraft may need additional distance to either stop safely (stopway) or continue to climb (clearway). The balanced field concept considers both.

q: 26. The minimum width of clearway is ............
explain: According to ICAO standards, the clearway should have a minimum width of 150 m, which is usually centered along the extended centerline of the runway.

q: 27. If the monthly mean of average daily temperature for the hottest month of the year is 25°C and the monthly mean of the maximum daily temperature of the same month of the year is 46°C, the airport reference temperature is ............
explain: Airport Reference Temperature $T_a = T_1 + \frac{T_2 - T_1}{3}$. Here, $25 + \frac{46 - 25}{3} = 25 + 7 = 32°C$.

q: 28. The total length of a runway is 1000 m. The elevation at distance 0, 200 m, 400 m, 600 m, 800 m and 1000 m are 100.0 m, 99.2 m, 101.0 m, 101.8 m, 101.4 m and 101.0 m respectively. The effective gradient of runway will be ............
explain: Effective Gradient is the maximum difference in elevation divided by total length. Max elevation is 101.8m and Min is 99.2m. $(101.8 - 99.2) / 1000 = 0.26\%$.

q: 29. The length of runway under standard conditions is 2500 m. The elevation of airport site is 300 m. Its reference temperature is 33.05°C. If the runway is to be constructed with an effective gradient of 0.25 percent, the corrected runway length will be ............
explain: Corrections are applied sequentially: 1. Elevation (7% per 300m), 2. Temperature (1% per 1°C rise above standard), 3. Gradient (20% per 1% effective gradient). Total calculation leads to 2800m.

q: 30. As per I.C.A.O., the minimum basic runway length for A and E type of airport will be ............
explain: ICAO classifies 'A' type as >2100m and 'E' type as 600m for basic runway length requirements.

q: 31. The cruising speed of the aircraft is 500 kmph. If there a head wind of 50 kmph, then the air speed and ground speed of the aircraft respectively will be ............
explain: Air speed is relative to the air (500 kmph). Ground speed = Air speed - Head wind (500 - 50 = 450 kmph).

q: 32. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: F.I.R. stands for flight information regions
F.I.C stands for flight information centre
explain: All provided definitions for Flight Information Regions, Centres, and standard radii for control areas/zones are correct in aviation standards.

q: 33. If the visibility of environment is less than 4 KNm then pilot must follow
explain: When visibility falls below the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) limit, pilots must switch to Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).

q: 34. For determining the basic runway length, the landing case requires that aircraft should come to a stop within p% of the landing distance. The value of p is ............
explain: Safety regulations require that the aircraft must be able to land and stop within 60% of the available runway length.

q: 35. The coordinates of the ends of a runway are (5000, 5000) and (8000, 7000). The co-ordinates of the A.R.P are
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the geometric center. Calculation: (5000+8000)/2 = 6500 and (5000+7000)/2 = 6000.

q: 36. The bearing of the longest line of a wind rose is S 45° E. The bearing of the runway will be numbered
explain: S 45° E is 135°. The opposite end is 315°. Runway numbers are 135/10 ≈ 13 and 315/10 ≈ 31.

q: 37. Runway threshold is indicated by a series of parallel lines starting from a distance of ............
explain: Threshold stripes start 6 meters from the beginning of the runway to indicate the start of the landing area.

q: 38. The WCB of the 1st and 2nd end of the runway are 80° and 260° respectively. Find the runway number indicated on the 1st end
explain: The runway number for the 1st end is 80/10 = 8.

q: 39. *The bearing of the 1st end of straight runway is 90°. Find the runway number of 1st end
explain: The runway number is 90/10 = 9.

q: 40. The airplane of IAR was hijacked from Tribhuvan International Airport in
explain: Indian Airlines flight IC 814 was hijacked on Dec 24, 1999, after taking off from Kathmandu.

q: 41. The maximum number of airports is located in the district
explain: Solukhumbu district has the highest number of airports in Nepal including Lukla and Phaplu.

q: 42. Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal was established in
explain: CAAN was established as an autonomous body on Dec 31, 1998.

q: 43. The number of international airports in Nepal
explain: Nepal recognizes 4 international airports: TIA, GBIA, Pokhara, and Nijgadh (under project).

q: 44. For supersonic transport aircraft, the minimum turning radius of taxiway is ............
explain: Supersonic aircraft have longer wheelbases and higher speeds, requiring a larger turning radius of 180m.

q: 45. *The width of taxiway is kept about
explain: Generally, the width of the taxiway is kept roughly 1/2 of the runway width.

q: 46. The purposed international airport in Nepal is
explain: Nijgadh International Airport in Bara is the major proposed international airport.

q: 47. The National pride project concerned with airport is
explain: Nijgadh International Airport is a designated National Pride Project of Nepal.

q: 48. Lord Ram returned from Lanka to Ayodhya through
explain: According to Hindu mythology, the Pushpak Viman was used by Lord Ram.

q: 49. As the elevation of airport increases the runway length
explain: Higher elevation means thinner air, which reduces lift, requiring a longer runway for takeoff.

q: 50. The slope of the transitional surface for A, B and C type of runway shall be ............
explain: Transitional surfaces extend from the edge of the runway strip to the inner horizontal surface. For larger categories (A, B, C), the slope is 1:7.
